topic: Instruction Set Architecture (ISA) Differences: CISC vs. RISC
explanation: Instruction Set Architecture (ISA) defines the instructions a processor can execute.  CISC (Complex Instruction Set Computer) and RISC (Reduced Instruction Set Computer) represent contrasting design philosophies. CISC ISAs feature a large number of complex instructions with varying execution times, aiming for high-level language expressiveness. RISC ISAs employ a smaller, simpler instruction set with fixed execution times, prioritizing efficient hardware implementation and predictability.  This impacts performance, code size, and compiler complexity.
